title: Yields At 5.3%; Is Another 2008 Banking Crisis Next? | Ben Chabot
speaker: Ben Chabot (ex-Chicago Fed economist), interviewed by David Lin

macro_themes.view: He is more pessimistic than optimistic: yields have not reached equilibrium and should stay high and keep rising as long as the AI investment boom continues.

macro_themes.theme: Treasury can't control the long end
macro_themes.view: Small buybacks or jawboning only work at the margin; yield-curve control would be inflationary; cutting the deficit is what would help.
Round-number thresholds like 5% can coordinate investors into a high-rate, rising-debt equilibrium; not his base case for the US but possible.

As of the 2023-24 exploratory stress tests most large banks were well hedged and earn more when rates rise; the real risk is a steep curve inversion or deposits becoming rate-sensitive (e.g. AI agents).

macro_themes.theme: Rising term premium and policy path
macro_themes.view: Fed path has repriced ~100bp higher over the year and term premium is rising; weaker auction tails show buyers demanding more yield, but no failed auction, just higher rates.
Heavy long-duration AI/data-center borrowing must be absorbed by non-natural buyers, pushing yields up and crowding out other construction.

calls.condition: As long as the AI investment boom continues and the stock market stays high.
calls.reason: Supply of long-duration government and AI corporate debt exhausts natural buyers, so 'tourists' must be paid higher yields; policy path and term premium both rising.
calls.quote: I expect yields to stay high and keep rising
